mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for three consecutive weeks from -30.9 to -24.3, and this momentum persists as transit recovery lowers the cost of leisure trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -30.9 to -24.3 over weeks t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than the last 28-day mean of -27.3 despite both RETAIL_REC and TRANSIT having risen over the prior three weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL falls below 9.0, reduced time at home releases trips to non-essential retail; the threshold crossing from 9.0 to 8.3 in the last two weeks predicts higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 9.0 at t-2w to 8.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL falls below 9.0 but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than its last 14-day mean, the threshold mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of rising TRANSIT and falling WORKPLACES indicates leisure and mixed trips replacing commutes; this substitution raises RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks when TRANSIT rises while WORKPLACES falls week-on-week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises and WORKPLACES falls week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -36.0 to -34.7 while WORKPLACES fell from -29.4 to -32.3 in the last week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than its last 14-day mean in weeks when TRANSIT rises and WORKPLACES falls week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS falling from -0.6 to -6.9 signals adverse late-winter weather, pushing outdoor activity indoors; this substitution lifts RETAIL_REC over the next week when PARKS is below -5.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -0.6 at t-2w to -6.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS is below -5 but RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is not higher than its prior 7-day mean, weather-substitution is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Post-restriction reopening allows TRANSIT recovery to feed high-street footfall; when TRANSIT exceeds -35, retail mobility rises over the next four weeks as policy constraints continue to ease.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -41.6 to -34.7 over the four weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT exceeds -35 but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not above its last 28-day mean, the policy-reopening channel is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM stabilising near -8.4 indicates the end of precautionary stockpiling, freeing household trip budgets for discretionary retail; this predicts higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -10.6 to -8.4 over the four weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM is above -9 and RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than its last 14-day mean, the normalisation mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The last-week drop in WORKPLACES from -29.4 to -32.3 signals renewed remote work, reducing weekday commuter footfall and pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -29.4 at t-1w to -32.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES falls week-on-week but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than its last 14-day mean, the remote-work drag is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL declines and TRANSIT rises together, households shift from home to out-of-home leisure, creating a compounded lift in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 9.0 and TRANSIT rises above -35
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 9.0 to 8.3 while TRANSIT rose from -37.9 to -34.7 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL is below 9.0 and TRANSIT is above -35 but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not above its last 28-day mean, the interaction is rejected.
